get.description: Every parameter of one captured group.

The instance classes AWS offers for an engine version: of a resource, or one a create chose.

With `resource_id`, the engine and version are the instance's, cluster's or snapshot's (a snapshot for the
restore form). Without one (an instance or cluster create), `engine` and `engine_version` say what to
ask about, in `target_key` or else the environment's first target.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    environment_slug: Environment the resource or the create belongs to.
    resource_id: Resource id of the instance, cluster or snapshot; None for a create.
    engine: `postgres` or `aurora-postgresql`, when no resource is given.
    engine_version: The version, such as `16.4`, when no resource is given.
    target_key: The target a create puts its resource in; the environment's first target when None.

Returns:
    The orderable classes, sorted; an empty list when the simulated account cannot answer.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an id that is not a resource id, a resource missing from the latest inventory
        of the environment, or an unknown environment or target; 422 when the resource is not an
        instance, cluster or snapshot, or neither a resource nor an engine and version is given; 502,
        with the diagnosis, when AWS fails.

Example:
    GET /api/v1/lifecycle/instance-classes?environment_slug=sandbox&resource_id=... returns
    `{"classes": ["db.m6g.large", "db.m6g.xlarge"]}`; so does
    `?environment_slug=sandbox&engine=postgres&engine_version=16.4`.

The window a point-in-time restore of an instance or cluster can choose a time from.

Read from the latest inventory (`LatestRestorableTime`, and `EarliestRestorableTime` or the creation time
and backup retention); nothing is asked of AWS. The point-in-time restore checks a chosen time against
the same window.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    resource_id: Resource id of the instance or cluster.

Returns:
    Both times as ISO 8601 UTC, or nulls with the reason when the inventory cannot say.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an id that is not a resource id or a resource missing from the latest
        inventory; 422 when the resource is not an instance or cluster.

Example:
    GET /api/v1/lifecycle/restore-window/<id> returns
    `{"earliest_utc": "2026-10-04T09:55:00Z", "latest_restorable_utc": "2026-10-11T09:55:00Z",
    "unknown_reason": null}`.

Most recent first.

Without `environment_slug` the list covers every environment and the operations that belong to none
(environment imports). `kind` keeps one operation kind (`operation_kind` is the same filter by its older
name); `kind=environment_import` finds imports even with an `environment_slug`, since an import belongs
to no environment. `resource_id` keeps the operations on one resource (a value from a resource page or
an operation row); `state` keeps the given states, one or several separated by commas (`RUNNING`, or
`QUEUED,RUNNING,AWAITING_APPROVAL` for everything in progress). A queued, running or awaiting-approval
row carries `progress` (completed and total steps, the current step) when its kind has an executor.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 when `resource_id` is malformed, or `kind` and `operation_kind` differ.

get.description:
Compare a parameter group with its family's defaults or with another group.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    left: Resource id of the left parameter group.
    right: Resource id of the right parameter group; the family defaults when omitted.
    against_defaults: Compare with the family defaults even when `right` is given.

Returns:
    One row per parameter overridden on either side (every family parameter against defaults), with the
    two values, the family default, whether they differ and whether the parameter needs a reboot.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an id that is not a resource id or a group missing from the latest inventory
        (or a family neither cached nor bundled); 422 when a resource is not a parameter group.

Engine versions with families and upgrade targets.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    environment_slug: Environment whose first target is asked (a simulated one answers from the bundle).
    engine: `postgres` or `aurora-postgresql`.

Returns:
    The engine's versions, each with its parameter group family and valid upgrade targets.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an unknown environment; 502, with the diagnosis, when AWS fails.

Metadata for a family's instance or cluster parameter groups, through the environment's first target.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    family: Parameter group family, e.g. `postgres16`.
    environment_slug: Environment whose first target is asked (a simulated one answers from the bundle).
    scope: `instance` for instance parameter groups (the default), `cluster` for cluster parameter
        groups; an Aurora family lists other parameters for each.

Returns:
    The parameters that groups of that family and scope have, with allowed values and apply types, and
    whether AWS or the bundle supplied them.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an unknown environment or family; 502, with the diagnosis, when AWS fails.

post.description:
Classify the current overrides against the target family without changing anything.

Args:
    request: The incoming request.
    body: The instance or cluster and the version it will be upgraded to.

Returns:
    One plan per group an upgrade build would create (the instance group and, for a cluster, the
    cluster group): the source group, the new group's name and family, every override classified as
    carried, default changed, needing review, removed or renamed, and the parameters the new group would
    hold. Also the families the instance and cluster groups are built for.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 for an id that is not a resource id or a resource missing from the latest
        inventory; 422 when the groups cannot be worked out (the members of a cluster use different
        instance groups, or a family is unknown); 502, with the diagnosis, when AWS fails.

get.description:
